title: How Does a Thermostat Know When to Turn On? #Shorts
description:
How does a thermostat know when to turn on? Inside a classic round thermostat is a coil of brass and steel stuck together. Brass shrinks more in the cold, so as your room cools the coil curls tighter until its tip touches a metal contact, and that click starts the furnace. As the room warms the coil loosens and the heat shuts off. Turning the dial just moves the contact. And it only feels the air right next to it, so sun, a lamp or a draft can fool it.
